pairs.why: A is a wall clock hung flat, like the real card, while B's round clock stands on the floor with no stand or foot and would roll over.
A's keypad has no '=' key (a wide 0 takes its place), so the calculator could not work, while B has a complete key layout.
B is a sound four-wheel wagon with smaller front wheels and a tongue, while A's single wheel pair and loose-looking shaft are less clearly attached and supported.
A's X-frame camp chair hangs together, while in B the back frame does not join the seat properly and the front seat tube sticks out past the frame.
A's lifebuoy hangs from its post on a rope, while B's lifebuoy stands upright around a post that goes through the deck, which is impossible.
B is a properly wall-hung clock, while A's round clock stands on the floor with no stand to hold it up.
B's chessboard has a sensible grid on a solid pedestal, while A's board has an oversized, irregular number of squares.
B is a coherent four-wheel covered wagon, while A has a bench stuck onto the box edge and an oddly angled single shaft lying on the ground with a crossbar.
